description: space.rs:274-286, 304-322 (and similar) — closures inside .iter().map() carry explicit type annotations: '|m: &SpaceAddMemberInput<'_>| -> Result<serde_json::Value, jmap_base_client::ClientError> { ... }'. Type inference works from the outer .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>() (which is itself fine), but the explicit annotations are necessary because the closure body has an early 'return Err(...)' that ambiguates the closure's Result type. Engineering basis: noisy. The cleaner Rust idiom is to restructure to avoid the early return — convert the if-guard to a let-else with a Result chain, or use 'if c.name.is_empty() { Err(...) } else { Ok(...) }' as a tail expression. Counter-argument: the explicit annotation is documentation — it says 'this closure produces a Result<Value, ClientError>' which a reader appreciates. Marking opinion because the engineering basis is contested — type-inference brevity vs explicit-annotation documentation is a genuine preference axis.
title: space.rs map closures carry redundant explicit type annotations
